entry.title: Playa de Benicassim
entry.summary: Benicassim has a long strip of golden sand and pebbles on the Orange Blossom Coast, backed by a promenade of old villas. The water is calm and shallow, and the coast is known for its summer music festival.

entry.title: Bibione Beach
entry.summary: Bibione has a wide beach of fine sand stretching along the Adriatic coast between the Tagliamento and Livenza rivers. The water is shallow and warm, and rows of umbrellas line the shore.

entry.title: Durres Beach
entry.summary: Durres has a long beach of grey sand along the Adriatic coast, close to Albania largest port and the ruins of the Roman amphitheatre. The water is warm and shallow, and the promenade is lively in summer.

entry.title: Praia da Vagueira
entry.summary: Praia da Vagueira is a long, wide Atlantic beach of golden sand backed by dunes, near the lagoon of Aveiro. It is quieter than the better known beaches of the Algarve, with strong waves that suit surfers.

entry.title: Praia da Figueira da Foz
entry.summary: The beach of Figueira da Foz is famously wide, with a long stretch of fine golden sand beside the mouth of the Mondego river. Atlantic waves roll in, and the city promenade is just behind.

entry.title: Plage du Bon-Secours, Saint-Malo
entry.summary: Plage du Bon-Secours lies just below the granite walls of Saint-Malo, with a famous tidal swimming pool built on the rocks. The tides are huge here, and at low tide the beach stretches far out toward the islets.

entry.title: Plage de Saint-Jean-de-Luz
entry.summary: Saint-Jean-de-Luz has a calm, curved bay of fine sand protected by sea walls, with a lively promenade and Basque houses behind. The water is gentle and safe for swimming, unlike the open surf beaches nearby.

entry.title: Plage des Sablettes, Menton
entry.summary: Plage des Sablettes is the favourite beach of Menton, a short stretch of grey pebbles with calm water and the pastel houses of the old town rising behind. The Italian border is a short walk to the east.

entry.title: Plage de Sainte-Maxime
entry.summary: The main beach of Sainte-Maxime is a long stretch of fine sand on the gulf of Saint-Tropez, with calm shallow water and a view across the bay to the old town of Saint-Tropez. The town is lively and easy to walk.

entry.title: Spiaggia Guidi, Carloforte
entry.summary: Spiaggia Guidi is a small sandy cove on the island of San Pietro, off the south-west coast of Sardinia. The water is clear and calm, and the shore is backed by low scrub, far from the crowds of the main island.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Marzamemi
entry.summary: Marzamemi is an old tuna-fishing village on the south-east tip of Sicily, and the beaches around it are sandy and shallow, with very clear water. The village square and the old tuna works give the place a unique character.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Scalea
entry.summary: Scalea has a long beach of grey pebbles and sand along the Riviera dei Cedri on the northern Calabrian coast. The sea is clear and warm, and the hills behind the town rise steeply.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Marina di Maratea
entry.summary: Marina di Maratea is a small port with a pebble beach below steep green mountains, on the short Tyrrhenian coast of Basilicata. The water is very clear, and the cliffs above give shelter from the wind.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Sanremo
entry.summary: Sanremo has several public beaches of pebbles and sand along its Riviera coast, with calm water and palm trees on the promenade. The old town of La Pigna and the casino are within walking distance.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Peschici
entry.summary: Peschici is a whitewashed hill village on the Gargano coast, and its beach is a long stretch of fine sand below the old town. The water is shallow and clear, and the cliffs and pine woods of the Gargano frame the bay.

entry.title: Playa Arenal-Bol, Calpe
entry.summary: Arenal-Bol is the main beach of Calpe, a wide stretch of fine sand with the great rock of Penon de Ifach rising behind it. The water is calm and clear, and the promenade is lined with cafes.

entry.title: Playa del Arenal, Javea
entry.summary: Playa del Arenal is the main beach of Javea, a long crescent of fine sand with clear water and a lively promenade. The Montgo mountain and the cape of San Antonio frame the view.

entry.title: Playa de Les Marines, Denia
entry.summary: Les Marines is a long, flat beach of dark sand north of Denia, with calm shallow water and very gentle slopes. The Montgo mountain stands behind, and the beach is quieter than the resorts further south.

entry.title: Playa de Peniscola
entry.summary: Peniscola has a long, gently shelving beach of fine sand facing the sea, with the white castle of the Templars rising on a rocky headland beside it. The water is warm and shallow, so it suits families.

entry.title: Platja Gran, Tossa de Mar
entry.summary: Platja Gran is the main beach of Tossa de Mar, a crescent of golden sand overlooked by the medieval walls and towers of the Vila Vella. The water is clear and the setting is among the prettiest on the Costa Brava.

entry.title: Platja de Lloret
entry.summary: The main beach of Lloret de Mar is a wide bay of coarse golden sand, framed by rocky headlands and a promenade. It is lively and busy in summer, with calm water and a steep slope near the shore.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Sabaudia
entry.summary: The beach of Sabaudia is a long, wide stretch of fine sand backed by dunes and the Circeo national park. The promontory of Monte Circeo closes the view to the south, and the sea is clear and gently shelving.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Gabicce Mare
entry.summary: Gabicce Mare is a family resort at the northern end of the Marche coast, with a long beach of fine sand and warm shallow water. The cliffs of the San Bartolo park rise behind the town.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Sirolo
entry.summary: Sirolo is a hill town on the Conero Riviera, and its beaches are white pebble coves under steep green cliffs. The sea is clear and turquoise, and the nearest beach is a short walk from the town centre.

entry.title: Primosten Beach
entry.summary: Primosten sits on a small wooded islet joined to the mainland, with pebble beaches and clear water on both sides. The old town rises above the shore, and the coves are calm and easy to reach on foot.

entry.title: Jonufer Beach
entry.summary: Jonufer is a quiet stretch of coast just north of Vlora, where the Adriatic meets the Ionian Sea. The beach is a mix of sand and pebbles with clear water, and a few cafes serve fresh fish.

entry.title: Saranda Beach
entry.summary: Saranda is a lively port town on the Ionian coast, and its waterfront pebble beach looks across the strait to Corfu. The water is clear, and the promenade is lined with cafes and restaurants.

entry.title: Umag Beach
entry.summary: Umag sits on a small peninsula on the north-west coast of Istria, and its beaches are a mix of pebbles, rocks and concrete platforms. The sea is clean and calm, and the old town is a short walk away.

entry.title: Crikvenica Beach
entry.summary: Crikvenica has several kilometres of pebble and shingle beach along its seafront promenade on the Kvarner coast. The water is clear and shallow, with sections of sand and concrete platforms for sunbathing.

entry.title: Grande Plage de Quiberon
entry.summary: The Grande Plage of Quiberon is a sheltered curve of sand facing the bay, with calm water and a seafront lined with cafes. It is on the Quiberon peninsula, which is known for its wild coast on the other side.
